headline: AI optimism lifts futures ahead of Fed chair's Jackson Hole test
body: Futures point to a firmly risk-on open Thursday, led by the Nasdaq 100, after Nvidia's latest quarter beat estimates again -- revenue roughly doubled year-over-year -- and management guided to continued strong growth into fiscal 2027, quieting worries that AI capital spending was topping out. The stock's own move was muted on the print itself, consistent with a pattern of underwhelming post-earnings pops despite strong numbers, but the guidance was enough to lift the broader semiconductor and tech complex in early trading. A stronger-than-expected durable goods report, with orders up 1.1% against forecasts near 0.4% and an acceleration from July, added a second tailwind. Small caps lagged the mega-cap-led advance, with the Russell 2000 roughly flat, suggesting breadth remains narrow even as headline sentiment brightens.

The bigger swing factor is still a day away: new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole address Friday morning, and positioning looks tentative into it -- most surveyed fund managers expect a neutral tone, but Warsh has broken from the prior Fed's habit of pre-signaling policy, so the speech carries real information risk in either direction, especially with inflation still running above target while the labor market softens. That undercurrent of caution shows up elsewhere: consumer confidence slipped to a seven-month low as mortgage rates ground higher and loan demand weakened, a reminder that the resilient-spending story isn't universal. Retail chatter is more stock-specific than macro today -- Nvidia and Google dominate trending boards alongside a sharp mention spike in Nike -- so the read leans more on price action and the data calendar than on any coordinated social-sentiment shift.
